claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: Failing scans unconditionally when the index is behind the tip breaks scans for ranges that are already available.
claims.quote: There we don't fail unconditionally if the index isn't synced. We only fail if we the range isn't available.

status_by.quote: You're right - thanks. getblockfilter does not fail merely because index is behind the tip, so it fails when the requested filter isn't available

claims.status_note: author updated to mirror getblockfilter and only fail when the requested range is unavailable

claims.author: fjahr
claims.quote: This doesn't make sense, you are waiting for the index to be synced just to delete it without doing anything else.
claims.request: Remove the redundant wait for the index to sync right before deleting it.

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: The functional test mines an excessive number of blocks.
claims.quote: No normal functional test should require mining this many blocks.

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: The functional test relies on races and is non-deterministic.
claims.quote: And we don't leave the actual testing to chance. The test either needs to work deterministically or it is of no use for us, with maybe some very rare exceptions.

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: Index readiness checked before the scan begins may become outdated by the end of a long scan, leading to misclassified errors.
claims.quote: This status may be outdated at the end of a long scan.

claims.author: fjahr
claims.question: Why throw an error when a filter range is unavailable instead of returning a partial result?
claims.quote: Why throw here instead of returning a partial result?
